lines.en: of the so-called Centaur and the hind parts of the bull.

lines.en: And according to the Indians a beautiful and fortunate woman, caring for wealth,

lines.en: and eating much and seeking wealth and quarreling for the sake of it.

lines.text: Κατὰ δὲ Ἰνδοὺς κύων καὶ λυκοπάνθηρος καὶ χοῖρος ἄγριος καὶ
lines.en: And according to the Indians a dog and a wolf-panther and a wild pig and

lines.text: πάρδος μέγας λευκόθριξ καὶ ἀγρίμια διάφορα κατοικοῦντα ἐν βάλταις.
lines.en: a great white-haired pard and various wild beasts dwelling in swamps.

lines.text: Κατὰ δὲ Πτολεμαῖον τὸ στῆθος τῆς μικρᾶς ἄρκτου καὶ ἡ λοξότης

lines.en: of the dragon and a man kneeling and the arm of the southern

lines.text: ὀφιούχου καὶ ἡ κοιλία τοῦ λέοντος καί ἡ ἀρχὴ τοῦ θυτηρίου.
lines.en: serpent-bearer and the belly of the lion and the beginning of the altar.

lines.text: Ὁ δὲ Τοξότης ἐστὶ ζῷον δισώματον καὶ ἐλλεῖπον κατὰ τὸ μῆκος
lines.en: And Sagittarius is a double-bodied animal and lacking in length

lines.text: καὶ διχότομον.
lines.en: and cut in two.

sections.en: 5 λέοντος ('of the lion') namely the beast carried by the Centaur. 6 λέοντος ('of the lion') the codex has falsely for σκορπίου ('of the scorpion'). 11 οὐρᾶς τοῦ Ὠρίωνος ('of the tail of Orion') : falsely the Byzantine for 'aššugâ' (hydra) placed 'aššagâ' (strong, i.e. Orion) (Dyroff). 12 λέοντος ('of the lion') again the codex has falsely for σκορπίου ('of the scorpion'). 16 ὄφεως ('of the serpent'): that this virgin with the serpent is Hygiea shines forth even more clearly from Varahamihira, who describes this figure thus: 'a woman wrapped around by serpents'. You see that he, who invented that Indian Sphere, introduced the gods of the Greeks. Concerning Hygiea transfigured into the constellation of Ophiuchus, cf. Sphaera, p. 113 sq. 20 ὀφιούχου ('of Ophiuchus') falsely for βοώτου ('of Bootes') as already above p. 164, 28. 21 λέοντος ('of the lion') the codex has. 23 δάκνυντα ('biting') the codex has; cf. p. 168, 23. ἰχθύας ('fishes') by a frequent error for serpents is used even in the Latin versions of Apomasar (namely Arab. 'ḥîtân' (fishes) for 'ḥajjatân' (two serpents), as Dyroff notes. 28 νοτίου ('southern') error of the interpreter for δεξιός ('right') (βραχίων ('arm')). 29 λέοντος ('of the lion') : read σκορπίου ('of the scorpion'). 30 ἔνιπον (?) ('I rebuked'?) the codex has : ἐλλεῖπον ('lacking') I have written ('unvollständig' Dyroff translates from the Arab.) : ἔλλιπον ('lacking') the interpreter seems to have said.

summary.headline: Scorpio Decans and Co-Rising Figures
summary.text: Descriptions of the three decans of Scorpio and their co-rising figures according to the Indians and Ptolemy, including Asclepius, Centaur, hare, fishes, wild beasts, and associated stellar parts; the concluding note characterizes Sagittarius as a truncated, double-bodied animal. Footnotes discuss Hygiea, Ophiuchus, Varahamihira, Apomasar, and textual errors in the codex.
